section: Social and religious reform in Andhra - Kandukuri Veeresalingam, Gurajada Apparao, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu

accepted.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was inspired to join the Brahmo Samaj by whom?
accepted.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Brahmo Samaj under the inspiration of Pandit Sivanath Sastri.
accepted.tq: Test the reformer–influence association directly.

accepted.s: Which of the following regions was NOT specifically associated with the extension of Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu's reform activities from the Godavari districts?
accepted.x: His reform activities spread to the North Coastal Andhra districts of Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and Srikakulam, not Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Find the one location outside the stated reform area.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu:
1. He founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in 1891.
2. He was associated with the anti-nautch movement in Madras.
3. He founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry was associated with Desiraju Peda Bapayya.
accepted.tq: Separate the reformer's own organisations from those founded by another reformer.

accepted.s: Which one of the following journals was associated with the anti-Devadasi campaign of Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu?
accepted.x: People's Friend was associated with Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu's anti-Devadasi campaign.
accepted.tq: Match the reform journal with its distinctive social campaign.

accepted.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu held the office of Vice-Chancellor of Madras University during which period?
accepted.x: The stated tenure of Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu as Vice-Chancellor of Madras University was 1925–1928.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed tenure periods.

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was conferred on Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu in 1932?
accepted.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu received the title 'Brahmarshi' in 1932.
accepted.tq: Test the title–year association.

accepted.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu received a knighthood in 1924 and was the first person of which category to receive it?
accepted.x: He was the first non-official educator to receive a knighthood, in 1924.
accepted.tq: Use the precise description rather than the associated titles.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Association)
 a. Social Purity Association
 b. Widow Remarriage Association
 c. Temperance and Social Purity Sangham
 d. Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj

List-II (Founder)
 i. Gidugu Ramamurthy
 ii. Desiraju Peda Bapayya
 iii. R. Venkataratnam Naidu
 iv. Kandukuri Veeresalingam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The correct associations are Social Purity Association–R. Venkataratnam Naidu; Widow Remarriage Association–Veeresalingam; Temperance and Social Purity Sangham–Desiraju Peda Bapayya; and Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj–Gidugu Ramamurthy.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure founder–association pairs.

accepted.s: The Social Purity Association, also known as Samajika Shuddhi Samajam, was founded in:
accepted.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu founded the Social Purity Association in 1891.
accepted.tq: Test the association–year pair directly.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj — Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu
Temperance and Social Purity Sangham — Desiraju Peda Bapayya
Social Purity Association — R. Venkataratnam Naidu
accepted.x: The Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj was founded by Gidugu Ramamurthy, not Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu.
accepted.tq: Use the swapped-founder trap in institutional history.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Vivekavardhini was associated with Rajahmundry in 1874. Manavaseva was published from Madras in 1911, while Satyasamvardhini and Dharmajyoti were associated with Rajahmundry and Kakinada respectively.
accepted.tq: Compare journals by both place and year.

accepted.s: The journal Dharmajyoti was associated with which place and year?
accepted.x: Dharmajyoti was associated with Kakinada and appeared in 1939.
accepted.tq: Test a journal’s place–year combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations regarding Brahmo magazines is correct?
accepted.x: Manavaseva was associated with Madras and appeared in 1911. Satyasamvardhini was associated with Rajahmundry, Dharmasadani with Sadhanashramam at Kakinada, and Dharmajyoti with Kakinada in 1939.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking both location and date.

accepted.s: The London Missionary Society established its centre at Jammalamadugu in:
accepted.x: The London Missionary Society established its Jammalamadugu centre in 1805.
accepted.tq: Match the mission with its earliest stated Andhra centre and year.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s: Which of the following areas was associated with the American Baptist mission in Andhra?
accepted.x: The American Baptist mission was active in Rayalaseema and had schools in Guntur, Gurazala, Palnadu, Ongole and Nellore.
accepted.tq: Identify the mission from its spread of activities.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s: The American Baptist mission's activities in Rayalaseema are associated with which year?
accepted.x: The American Baptist mission was associated with Rayalaseema from 1835.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the mission establishment years.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Church Mission Society in Andhra:
1. It operated in the Krishna-Godavari region from 1841.
2. Its school at Machilipatnam was established in 1841.
3. The Machilipatnam school became a college in 1864.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Church Mission Society operated in the Krishna-Godavari region from 1841, and its Machilipatnam school of that year became a college in 1864.
accepted.tq: Retain the full institutional sequence from establishment to upgrade.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pennsylvania Synod — Guntur, Prattipadu and Nallapadu
accepted.x: The Church Mission Society operated in the Krishna-Godavari region and had a school at Machilipatnam; it was not confined to Palnadu.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that narrows a mission’s area incorrectly.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Christian mission schools in Andhra is correct?
o: They admitted only members of the upper castes.
They excluded children from socially disadvantaged communities.
They admitted only converts from Europe.
accepted.x: Christian mission schools admitted Sudras and Panchamas, thereby extending education beyond the traditional upper-caste groups.
accepted.tq: Test the social composition of institutional beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s: The first Telugu journal, Satyadoota, was associated with which mission centre?
accepted.x: Satyadoota, regarded as the first Telugu journal, was associated with a Christian mission at Bellary.
accepted.tq: Link the publication with its mission centre.
accepted.sec: Christian missions in Andhra - year and centre

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Annie Besant became President of the Theosophical Society.
B. Annie Besant joined the Theosophical Society.
C. The Central Hindu College was established at Benaras.
D. The Theosophical Society headquarters was established at Adyar.
accepted.x: The correct order is Adyar headquarters in 1882, Annie Besant's joining in 1893, Central Hindu College in 1898, and her presidency in 1907.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the two middle dates.

accepted.s: The Central Hindu College established by Annie Besant at Benaras in 1898 later formed the nucleus of:
accepted.x: The Central Hindu College at Benaras became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University, established in 1916.
accepted.tq: Test the institution–later university relationship.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Annie Besant is correct?
1. She became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at Calcutta in 1917.
2. She launched the Home Rule movement in 1916.
3. She was associated with the papers New India and Commonweal.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Annie Besant was associated with Home Rule in 1916, the papers New India and Commonweal, and the 1917 Calcutta Congress presidency.
accepted.tq: Combine a leader’s political role, publications and organisational activity.

accepted.s: Annie Besant founded the National College, also known as BT College, at:
accepted.x: Annie Besant founded the National College, or BT College, at Madanapalle.
accepted.tq: Test the institution–location association.

accepted.s: Which of the following was established by the Pithapuram Raja at Kakinada in association with reform activities?
accepted.x: The Pithapuram Raja established Karunalayam at Kakinada in 1909 in association with reform and welfare activities.
accepted.tq: Match the patron with his institution and location.

accepted.s: Karunalayam, established by the Pithapuram Raja, was described as:
o: The first Brahmo Samaj in Andhra
The first girls' school in Andhra
accepted.x: Karunalayam was described as the only orphanage in Andhra and also provided vocational education.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive numerical or superlative description.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the philanthropic activities of the Pithapuram Raja?
o: A contribution of Rs 1 lakh to the Brahma Dharma Prachara Nidhi
Founding the Theosophical Society at New York
accepted.x: The Pithapuram Raja supported orphan and vocational schools, Brahmopasana Mandiram and the Brahma Dharma Prachara Nidhi. The Theosophical Society was founded at New York by Blavatsky and Olcott.
accepted.tq: Separate a patron’s activities from an unrelated organisation’s foundation.

accepted.s: The second edition of Kanyasulkam published in 1909 was dedicated to:
accepted.x: The second edition of Kanyasulkam, published in 1909, was dedicated to Ananda Gajapati.
accepted.tq: Test the work–dedication association.

accepted.s: The first staging of Kanyasulkam was associated with which troupe and place?
accepted.x: Kanyasulkam was first staged by the Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham of Vizianagaram.
accepted.tq: Match the literary work with its first staging institution and place.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct publication and staging sequence for Kanyasulkam?
o: Written in 1890, first staged in 1892, published in 1897
Written in 1892, first staged in 1897, published in 1909
Written in 1897, first staged in 1890, published in 1892
Written in 1909, first staged in 1892, published in 1897
accepted.x: Kanyasulkam was written in 1890, first staged on 13 August 1892, and published in 1897 by Vavilla.
accepted.tq: Arrange the work’s composition, performance and publication stages.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Kanyasulkam is best described as:
o: A historical epic in classical Telugu
A social play in vyavaharika Telugu
accepted.x: Kanyasulkam is a social play written in vyavaharika Telugu and deals with social evils such as bride-price, child marriage and the plight of widows.
accepted.tq: Distinguish genre, language style and subject matter.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Saranga Dhara — Telugu novel — Rural social reform
Purnamma — Poem — Girl married off for money
Mutyala Saralu — Poetry — New lyrical metre
accepted.x: Saranga Dhara is an English poem written with Shyamala Rao and published in Indian Leisure Hour; it is not a Telugu novel.
accepted.tq: Use the genre-swapping trap among closely related literary works.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Diddubatu is regarded as:
o: The first modern Telugu short story
accepted.x: Diddubatu is regarded as the first modern Telugu short story and deals with social reform.
accepted.tq: Test the literary milestone and genre together.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Which work of Gurajada Apparao depicts a girl being married off for money?
accepted.x: Purnamma, also known as Puttadi Bomma Purnamma, depicts a girl being married off for money.
accepted.tq: Match the work with its specific social theme.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Mutyala Saralu?
o: An English poem published in Indian Leisure Hour
A poetry work that introduced a new lyrical metre of the same name
A social play in Srikakulam dialect
A short story regarded as the first modern Telugu short story
accepted.x: Mutyala Saralu is a poetry work that introduced a new lyrical metre bearing the same name.
accepted.tq: Separate similar literary works by genre and distinctive contribution.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Saranga Dhara, published in Indian Leisure Hour, was written in English by Gurajada Apparao along with:
accepted.x: Saranga Dhara was an English poem written by Gurajada Apparao with his brother Shyamala Rao.
accepted.tq: Test the co-author association in literary history.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s: Which of the following characters in Kanyasulkam is correctly matched with the description?
accepted.x: Madhuravani is portrayed as a reformed courtesan. Girisham is an educated fraud, Ramappa Pantulu is a hypocrite and Buchamma is a widow.
accepted.tq: Match characters with their precise roles and avoid swapped descriptions.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kanyasulkam is correct?
1. It uses the Srikakulam dialect.
2. Soujanya Rao is portrayed as a reformer.
3. Ramappa Pantulu is portrayed as a hypocrite.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kanyasulkam uses the Srikakulam dialect, presents Soujanya Rao as a reformer and Ramappa Pantulu as a hypocrite.
accepted.tq: Combine language, character and social-role clues in a literary text.
accepted.sec: Gurajada Apparao's literary works - genre and social theme
